name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 district lean makes a Democratic upset highly improbable
Jerry Carl's roughly 13-to-1 fundraising edge plus $547K in outside support
Prediction markets price Carl's win odds near 96%
No public polling; Clyde Jones Jr. lacks name recognition and resources
model.rationale: An R+17 district, a thirteen-to-one fundraising gap favoring Jerry Carl, and prediction markets pricing his odds near 96% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no public polling and a minimally funded opponent, only an extraordinary environment shift could make this competitive.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or a major scandal involving Carl could tighten the race, though the district's strong lean would still favor Republicans.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is a heavily Republican seat, and the open-seat general election reflects that. Republican Jerry Carl enters with a large financial operation: more than $1.1 million raised, $367,000 in the bank, and over half a million dollars in outside support. Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $90,000 with minimal cash on hand, little name recognition, and no outside backing on record.

No public polls cover the contest, and no expert raters have ranked it, but the available signals align: the district's strong Republican lean, the wide fundraising gap, and prediction markets putting Carl's chances around 96%. The realistic question is the size of the winning margin, not the winner. Even a substantially Democratic-favorable national environment would leave a large gap to close, and this race shows no signs of closing it.
